title: Tenant Visibility Gateway: Authorization proxy for analytics/usage endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The console currently serves analytics and usage views from a set of internal endpoints that assume the caller enforces tenant scoping. Product wants per-organization visibility controls for usage dashboards, datasets, and CSV exports. Existing heuristics have leaked rows in staging and are not expressive enough for cross-team roles (owner/admin/observer) or delegated service accounts.

Goal:
Build a Tenant Visibility Gateway (TVG) — a lightweight authorization proxy that centralizes permission checks for analytics endpoints and materialized usage views. TVG will: enforce tenant-scoped filters, map Console roles to analytics access predicates, cache allowlists for performance, and emit rich audit events for compliance.

Non-goals:
- Replace application-level permissions in other subsystems (authn remains upstream).
- Implement full attribute-based access control (ABAC) — we will support role predicates + tag-based dataset grants in v1.

Design summary:
1) Placement: TVG runs as a sidecar/service in the console backend tier (scalable via k8s HPA). All analytics/usage routes are routed through TVG via Istio routing rules (non-breaking proxy insertion).
2) Policy model: a compact RBAC schema:
   - roles: org_admin, org_billing, org_viewer, dataset_owner, service_account
   - resources: usage_dashboard, dataset, export_job, raw_logs
   - actions: read, list, export, annotate
   - grants: allow(role, resource, action, optional predicate)
3) Predicate mapping: predicates are simple SQL WHERE fragments (safe-compiled) produced from grant metadata (e.g., dataset=customer_x OR team IN (analytics)). TVG will translate grants to query filters and attach them as parameterized predicates for analytics queries or materialized view fetches.
4) Caching: a two-layer cache:
   - in-memory LRU of request->decision (short TTL, 30s) for burst protection
   - Redis-backed grants cache keyed by org_id with 5m TTL and eviction on grant changes (push invalidation via events)
5) Auditing: every decision emits a compact audit record to the observability topic with fields: org_id, principal_id, role, resource, action, decision, grant_ids, trace_id.
6) Fallthroughs: explicit deny by default; legacy fallback to previous behavior only under a "maintenance-mode" feature flag controlled by ops.

API and integration points:
- New middleware: console routes register with TVG via static discovery file during deploy. TVG exposes an HTTP /authorize endpoint that accepts {principal, org_id, resource, action, context} and returns {allowed, predicate_sql, grants}.
- Analytics runner integration: augment analytics query builder to accept a predicate fragment and bind values (no raw string concatenation).
- Export jobs: TVG returns an allow + export_filter for CSV generation; export service validates returned predicate before executing.

Migration and rollout plan:
Phase 1 (canary): Route read-only dashboard widgets through TVG for <10% of orgs. Monitor latency delta, cache hit rate, and audit volume.
Phase 2: Gradually expand to all read routes and dataset listing. Block export and raw_logs until cache warm.
Phase 3: Enforce for export and scheduled jobs; flip maintenance-mode off.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation and predicate generation with a SQL sanitizer harness.
- Integration tests that spin up a test TVG and console routes to validate filter semantics with Postgres test datasets.
- Performance regression tests to measure median 95th token latency increase for dashboard queries (target <5ms added).

Observability & Metrics:
- TVG: request_rate, decision_latency_ms_{p50,p95}, cache_hit_rate, deny_rate, audit_event_count
- Business metrics: dashboards_returned_rows_delta, export_size_delta, errors_by_org
- Dashboards and SLOs: 99.9% availability for TVG and p95 decision latency <50ms at baseline load.

Security considerations:
- Predicate fragments must be produced via templates and sanitized; no raw SQL coupling from user input.
- All audit logs are write-once to kafka topic with encryption-at-rest and KMS key rotation.
- Role grant propagation authenticated by signed events from Admin service (rotate keys monthly).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should predicate compilation be pushed to a compile-step in analytics runner (fewer round-trips) vs keeping all in TVG (simpler line-of-sight)?
- How expressive do we allow predicates (tag-joins vs simple equals) without killing cacheability?
- Operational cost of Redis cluster vs in-cluster watches for grant invalidation.

Links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/TVG+design+proposal
- Spec draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/tvg-spec-draft
- Perf harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4821

Acceptance criteria:
- TVG accepts authz checks and returns correct predicates for a curated test matrix of 18 scenarios (cross-org, delegated SA, owner overrides).
- End-to-end tests validate that no rows for other orgs are visible in dashboards or CSV exports in staging.
- Production rollout flips maintenance-mode off only after 2 full days with cache miss rate <5% and no regression alerts for p95 latency.

Follow-ups after v1:
- Add RBAC UIs in Console for dataset-level grants (PM ticket).
- Evaluate ABAC pilot for sensitive datasets.
- Add per-grant TTL and expiration UI for short-lived service account grants.
